question.problem:
The joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given in the table below. Find $\text{E}[{X}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡Y].$

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=e$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.15$ | $0.3$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.35$ | $0.2$ |
question.worked_solution:
Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are discrete random variables with supports ${S}_{X}$ and ${S}_{Y},$ respectively, and $f(x,y)$ is their joint probability mass function with support $S={S}_{X}\times {S}_{Y}.$ If $r:{R}^{2}\to R$ is a function of two variables, then the rule of the lazy statistician states that

$$
\text{E}[r(X,Y)]={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}r(x,y)\,f(x,y).
$$

In our case, we have

$$
r(x,y)={x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡y.
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡Y] & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}r(x,y)\,f(x,y) \\  & =({1}^{2}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡1)\cdot f(1,1)+({1}^{2}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡e)\cdot f(1,e)+({2}^{2}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡1)\cdot f(2,1)+({2}^{2}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡e)\cdot f(2,e) \\  & =0\cdot f(1,1)+1\cdot f(1,e)\text{ }+0\cdot f(2,1)+4\cdot f(2,e) \\  & =0\cdot 0.15+1\cdot 0.3+0\cdot 0.35+4\cdot 0.2 \\  & =0+0.3+0+0.8 \\  & =1.1.\end{aligned}
$$
